Hi Sanjay — thanks for the trace and the heads-up. We're actively investigating and I've opened an internal incident (INF-4521). Short answers for immediate mitigation while we triage: 

1) Switch to non-streaming response (consolidated response) for the impacted route: set streaming=false or response_mode=full in your SDK calls. That avoids chunking latency tradeoffs.

2) Reduce client-side buffer/wait: set "buffer_ms" to 20 and "max_chunk_tokens" to 64 temporarily to reduce burstiness.

3) Temporary model fallback: if you can tolerate slightly different tokenization, route to rw-medium-1 for low-latency-critical sessions — we can bind a traffic policy for you.

4) If you must stay on streaming, add a short client-side timeout and auto-retry with exponential backoff (start 500ms). This prevents long idle periods from blocking the UX.

We are collecting telemetry; can you also send a sample request_id from an impacted session (X-Request-ID header) so we can correlate? I've attached our telemetry export (redwood-telemetry-rib-20260528.log) and asked SRE to look at token-delivery timing and inter-chunk gaps.

I'll update you in 30 minutes with our findings and a more durable workaround. We will also propose a make-good (credit) and a short post-incident write-up with root cause and hard actions.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: token-stream latency on 2026-05-28 — findings and next steps

Hi Sanjay — following up with a concise summary after our investigation and remediation. Thank you for your patience while we completed the root-cause analysis. Below is a short timeline, impact, and actions we will take.

Summary timeline
- 07:48 PDT — first elevated inter-chunk gaps observed for FinBridge live-assist sessions.
- 07:50–08:20 PDT — elevated latency window; a subset of requests experienced 1–4s pauses between chunks; some clients reverted to polling.
- 08:26 PDT — we received your initial report and began targeted correlation.
- 09:12 PDT — SRE identified a hot-spot in the caching layer (KV cache) causing write stalls during concurrent checkpoint writes under burst load.
- 11:00 PDT — engineering deployed a hotfix to mitigate write contention and added guardrails.
- 13:15 PDT — normal token cadence restored for impacted clusters.

Root cause (short):
Concurrent checkpoint writes to a shared KV cache under an unusual burst pattern triggered internal backpressure that delayed token emission on the streaming path. The latency manifested as multi-second inter-chunk gaps for affected requests.

Immediate mitigations we applied
- Applied a temporary token-emission buffer smoothing patch to the runtime to avoid long idle waits between chunks.
- Throttled background checkpointing on impacted hosts and prioritized streaming traffic.
- Enabled an account-level routing rule to move FinBridge traffic to an isolated low-latency pool while we complete a durable fix.

Customer guidance (recommended for your stack)
- If you see another brief blip, flip impacted critical sessions to response_mode=full for the shortest outage window.
- If streaming is required, keep buffer_ms low and implement short client-side timeouts + retry logic.
- Consider an account-level routing rule (we can automate this) to pin mission-critical traffic to our low-latency pool.

Longer-term actions (we will deliver within 30 days)
- Replace the KV checkpointing pattern with an append-only sync that avoids coordinated writer stalls.
- Add proactive detection and auto-failover for token-delivery stalls.
- Improve our telemetry surface so we alert internally on token-interarrival variance for top customers.

Make-good and next steps
- We're proposing a one-time billing credit; draft attached (sla-credit-draft.pdf). We will finalize after you confirm the impacted invoice period.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute review call this week to walk through the postmortem and field any technical Qs.
- Follow-up ticket: INF-4521 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521).

Again, very sorry for the disruption. We know predictable latency is table stakes for your customer flows; we've prioritized both a code fix and operational changes to prevent recurrence. Please reply with a preferred time for the review call and a sample request_id if you still have one.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
